claims.text: In June 2024, TfL recorded in-cab noise levels of 82 dB LAeq westbound from Mile End to Bethnal Green and 86 dB LAeq from Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street.

citations.quote: these measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab.
Mile End to Bethnal Green | 82
Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street | 86

claims.text: In TfL's June 2024 in-cab measurements, the eastbound noise level from Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green exceeded Bethnal Green to Mile End by 4 dB LAeq.

Our uncalibrated passenger saloon audio recordings showed an uncalibrated mean level of -18.66 dBFS(A) eastbound from Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green and -19.42 dBFS(A) from Bethnal Green to Mile End.
Across 11 paired trips, Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green was louder than Bethnal Green to Mile End by an uncalibrated mean contrast of 0.54 dB.
An indicative sound level meter app recording across one whole trip including dwell times showed 91.9 dB(A) LAeq eastbound between Liverpool Street and Mile End.
An indicative sound level meter app recording across one whole trip including dwell times showed 87.3 dB(A) LAeq westbound between Mile End and Liverpool Street.
A secondary press report citing JRPass attributed an average noise level of 92.8 decibels to Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green rather than TfL directly.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (Central line) – 92.8 decibels
Daniel de Nieuwe, Head of Product from JRPass said:

claims.text: Public records do not show whether rail grinding was carried out in both directions on these sections in subsequent years, nor whether the planned deep Tube reconditioning was completed.

Because our saloon recordings are uncalibrated and indicative app readings face microphone limitations at higher sound levels, our data cannot be compared directly like-for-like with TfL in-cab figures.
In July 2026, London Assembly Member Elly Baker reported that TfL turned down requests for specific Tube noise data.

citations.quote: turning down the majority of the requests for data

asks.request: Provide complete historical dates, running directions, and completion records for all rail grinding and deep Tube reconditioning carried out on the Central line between Liverpool Street, Bethnal Green, and Mile End from June 2022 to the present.
asks.why: Existing disclosures only confirm past grinding up to May 2022 and planned works for 2023/24, leaving it unclear what maintenance took place and in which directions (claims claim_1, claim_2, claim_13).

asks.request: Disclose TfL's bi-monthly in-cab noise monitoring logs for all Central line tunnel sections from June 2024 to date, alongside any corresponding passenger saloon acoustic measurements.
asks.why: TfL's disclosed section-level data is limited to June 2024 cab readings, preventing the London Assembly from tracking ongoing noise trends or assessing conditions in passenger carriages (claims claim_5, claim_6, claim_14).

asks.request: Clarify the methodology, dates, and measurement locations behind the 92.8 dB figure cited in public media for the Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green section.
asks.why: The widely reported 92.8 dB figure stems from a third-party product head rather than TfL's official disclosures, requiring formal clarification of whether TfL data was the source (claim claim_12).
